title: Tech Note: Printing Barcodes using 4D v11 SQL and SVG
author: Thomas Maul, General Manager, 4D Germany
featured_technology: Industrial 2 of 5, Code128, EAN, UPC encoding

historical_commentary.text: This note documents an update to an earlier barcode-generation technique (TN 05-08 for 4D v9), leveraging the new SVG capabilities introduced in 4D v11 SQL to replace the older 4D Chart-based approach. SVG offered superior speed and print quality, and the solution was packaged as a reusable compiled component (Barcode.4dbase) installable via 4D's component folder—a pattern that became standard practice for library distribution before modern package managers. The note also documents a bug fix for Code 128 lowercase 'g' character rendering. While SVG remains a standard web/graphics format, barcode generation itself has evolved toward dedicated libraries and external APIs, making this 4D-specific component approach largely historical.
related_updates: SVG support in 4D v11 SQL has evolved; modern 4D uses 4D View Pro (v18+) for advanced graphics
Component-based library distribution was later supplemented by the Package Manager (v18+)
Barcode generation is now often delegated to external services or dedicated JS libraries rather than server-side generation
The specific barcode formats supported (Code128, EAN-13, UPC-A, etc.) remain industry standards but implementation methods have diversified
